documents.prompt: A relation contains $({{x1}},{{y1}})$, $({{x2}},{{y2}})$, and $({{x3}},{{y3}})$. Which statement is true?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: The inputs {{x1}}, {{x2}} and {{x3}} are all different, so the relation is a function.
reasoning: A relation is a function when no input is paired with two different outputs.
The inputs (first coordinates) of $({{x1}},{{y1}})$, $({{x2}},{{y2}})$ and $({{x3}},{{y3}})$ are {{x1}}, {{x2}} and {{x3}}: no input repeats.
So each input has exactly one output. The relation is a function because each input is paired with exactly one output.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking the outputs must all be different, or that negative coordinates matter. Outputs may repeat; only one input with two different outputs breaks a function.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The relation is a function because each input is paired with exactly one output.

choices.label: The relation is a function because each input is paired with exactly one output.
The relation is not a function because the outputs are not required to be different.
The relation is not a function because some coordinates may be negative.
The relation is a function only if all three outputs are positive.

documents.prompt: A relation contains $({{x}},{{y1}})$ and $({{x}},{{y2}})$, where {{y1}} and {{y2}} are different. Can this relation define $y$ as a function of $x$?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: The input {{x}} is paired with both {{y1}} and {{y2}}, so this is not a function.
reasoning: For $y$ to be a function of $x$, each input may have only one output.
Both $({{x}},{{y1}})$ and $({{x}},{{y2}})$ have the input {{x}}, and their outputs differ: ${{y1}}\ne {{y2}}$.
One input with two outputs: No, because the same input is paired with two different outputs.
solutionReview.commonError: Answering yes because the two pairs share an input. A shared input is exactly what breaks a function when the outputs differ; negative values never matter.
solutionReview.answerSummary: No, because the same input is paired with two different outputs.

choices.label: No, because the same input is paired with two different outputs.
Yes, because the two ordered pairs have the same input.
Yes, because every ordered pair has two coordinates.
No, because a function cannot contain negative values.

documents.prompt: The equation $y={{m}}x {{b|signed}}$ defines $y$ in terms of $x$. Which statement is true?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: Each $x$ gives one $y$ in $y={{m}}x {{b|signed}}$, so it is a function.
reasoning: A function gives exactly one output for each input.
Any input gives one output: for example, $x=1$ gives $y={{m}}(1) {{b|signed}}={{v1}}$, and no other value.
Multiplying by {{m}} and then adding the constant term always has one result. For every value of $x$, the equation gives exactly one value of $y$, so it defines a function.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking an equation with both $x$ and $y$ cannot be a function, or that the slope must be positive or the intercept 0. The slope {{m}} and the intercept {{b}} do not matter.
solutionReview.answerSummary: For every value of $x$, the equation gives exactly one value of $y$, so it defines a function.

choices.label: For every value of $x$, the equation gives exactly one value of $y$, so it defines a function.
It does not define a function because both $x$ and $y$ appear.
It defines a function only when the slope is positive.
It does not define a function unless the $y$-intercept is 0.

documents.prompt: For each positive number of gallons $g$, a pump operating at a constant rate takes exactly one amount of time $t$ to move $g$ gallons. Which statement best describes $t$ as a function of $g$?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: Each number of gallons takes exactly one time, so $t$ is a function of $g$.
reasoning: A function pairs each allowed input with exactly one output. Here the input is the number of gallons $g$ and the output is the time $t$.
The pump runs at a constant rate, so moving the same $g$ gallons always takes the same time: one value of $t$ for each $g$.
It is a function because each allowed value of $g$ corresponds to exactly one value of $t$.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking different units, or two quantities that both change, rule out a function. All that matters is that no input gets two outputs.
solutionReview.answerSummary: It is a function because each allowed value of $g$ corresponds to exactly one value of $t$.

choices.label: It is a function because each allowed value of $g$ corresponds to exactly one value of $t$.
It is not a function because time and gallons use different units.
It is a function only if $g=t$.
It is not a function because both quantities can change.

documents.prompt: Which relation defines $y$ as a function of $x$?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: Only the linear equation gives one $y$ for each $x$.
reasoning: A relation defines $y$ as a function of $x$ when each input $x$ has only one output $y$. Test each choice.
In $x=y^2+{{a}}$, both $y=1$ and $y=-1$ give $x=1^2+{{a}}=(-1)^2+{{a}}={{a1}}$: one input, two outputs. $y^2=x+{{a}}$ and the circle $x^2+y^2={{a}}^2+4$ also give two values of $y$ for one $x$.
In $y={{a}}x {{b|signed}}$, each $x$ is multiplied by {{a}} and then {{b}} is added: one output. So the function is $y={{a}}x {{b|signed}}$.
solutionReview.commonError: Picking an equation just because it has $x$ and $y$ in it. When $y$ is squared, $y$ and $-y$ share the same input.

choices.label: $y={{a}}x {{b|signed}}$

documents.prompt: The relation contains $({{x}},{{y}})$, $({{u}},{{v}})$, and $({{x}},k)$. What value of $k$ makes the relation a function?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: The input {{x}} already has the output {{y}}, so $k={{y}}$.
reasoning: The pairs $({{x}},{{y}})$ and $({{x}},k)$ share the input {{x}}.
The pair $({{u}},{{v}})$ has a different input, so it puts no condition on $k$.
A function allows only one output for each input, so the second output must equal the first: $k={{y}}$.
solutionReview.commonError: Thinking $k$ must be a new output, different from {{y}}. Repeating an output is allowed; repeating an input with a new output is not.

documents.prompt: The relation is represented by $x={{c}}$. Does this relation define $y$ as a function of $x$?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: The graph of $x={{c}}$ is a vertical line, so it is not a function.
reasoning: Every point on the graph of $x={{c}}$ has the input {{c}}; the graph is a vertical line.
For example, $({{c}},0)$ and $({{c}},1)$ are both on it, so the input {{c}} has the outputs 0 and 1.
No, because the single input $x={{c}}$ can be paired with more than one value of $y$.
solutionReview.commonError: Saying yes because $x$ is fixed or the graph is straight. One input with many outputs is exactly what a function forbids: a vertical line fails the vertical line test.
solutionReview.answerSummary: No, because the single input $x={{c}}$ can be paired with more than one value of $y$.

choices.label: No, because the single input $x={{c}}$ can be paired with more than one value of $y$.
Yes, because $x$ has a fixed value.
Yes, because the graph is a straight line.
No, because a function cannot contain a constant.

documents.prompt: The relation $x=y^2$ is restricted to $y\ge 0$. Under this restriction, does the relation define $y$ as a function of $x$ for $x\ge0$?
attemptFeedback: Use the defining relationship in the prompt and verify the result in the original representation.
supportHints: Translate the notation or condition into an equation or input-output statement before answering.

solutionReview.headline: With $y\ge 0$, each $x\ge 0$ has one $y$, so it is a function.
reasoning: Without the restriction, $x=y^2$ pairs $x=4$ with both $y=2$ and $y=-2$: two outputs.
With $y\ge 0$, only the nonnegative root is left, $y=\sqrt{x}$: now $x=4$ gives only $y=2$.
Yes. For each $x\ge0$, the restriction leaves exactly one nonnegative value of $y$.
solutionReview.commonError: Saying a squared variable can never be part of a function. The restriction removes the negative root, leaving one $y$ for each $x$.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Yes. For each $x\ge0$, the restriction leaves exactly one nonnegative value of $y$.

choices.label: Yes. For each $x\ge0$, the restriction leaves exactly one nonnegative value of $y$.
No. Squared variables can never be part of a function.
No. Each nonnegative $x$ has no corresponding value of $y$.
Yes, but only when $x=0$.
